standart.baslik: SEALING AND COATING COMPOUND, CORROSION INHIBITIVE

sinir.orijinal_metin: The base compound and curing agent shall be of uniform blend and shall be free of skins, lumps, and jelled or coarse particles. There shall be no separation of ingredients which cannot be readily dispersed by mechanical agitation or mixing by hand.

Unless otherwise specified in the contract or order, the color of the sealing compound shall be as furnished by the manufacturer (see 6.2). The curing agent, if furnished separately, shall be of contrasting color to facilitate mixing.
TABLE I. Nonvolatile content, minimum percent by weight: Type I = 84.
TABLE I. Nonvolatile content, minimum percent by weight: Type II = 92.
TABLE I. Nonvolatile content, minimum percent by weight: Type III = 65.
TABLE I. Nonvolatile content, minimum percent by weight: Type IV Class 1 = 90.
TABLE I. Nonvolatile content, minimum percent by weight: Type IV Class 2 = 95.
When tested as specified in 4.8.3, the flow measurement of the sealing compound shall be not less than 0.10 inch and not greater than 0.75 inch.

testler.test_adi: Application life – application time – Type I

sinir.orijinal_metin: The end of the application time shall be considered to be not greater than 2,500 poises for Type I, not less than 15 grams per minute for Type II, not greater than 300 poises for Type III, and not less than 30 grams per minute for Type IV, Class 1 or 50 grams per minute for Type IV Class 2.

testler.test_adi: Application life – application time – Type II

sinir.orijinal_metin: The end of the application time shall be considered to be not greater than 2,500 poises for Type I, not less than 15 grams per minute for Type II, not greater than 300 poises for Type III, and not less than 30 grams per minute for Type IV, Class 1 or 50 grams per minute for Type IV Class 2.

testler.test_adi: Application life – application time – Type III

sinir.orijinal_metin: The end of the application time shall be considered to be not greater than 2,500 poises for Type I, not less than 15 grams per minute for Type II, not greater than 300 poises for Type III, and not less than 30 grams per minute for Type IV, Class 1 or 50 grams per minute for Type IV Class 2.

sinir.orijinal_metin: The end of the application time shall be considered to be not greater than 2,500 poises for Type I, not less than 15 grams per minute for Type II, not greater than 300 poises for Type III, and not less than 30 grams per minute for Type IV, Class 1 or 50 grams per minute for Type IV Class 2.

The sealant shall squeeze out to a thickness no greater than 0.005 inch at the bolts when tested as specified in 4.8.6.
When tested as specified in 4.8.7, the Shore A-2 hardness of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 35 for Types I, II, and III or 30 for Type IV.
When tested as specified in 4.8.7, the Shore A-2 hardness of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 35 for Types I, II, and III or 30 for Type IV.
When tested as specified in 4.8.8, the specific gravity of the cured sealing compound shall be not greater than 1.65 for Class 1 or 1.50 for Class 2.
When tested as specified in 4.8.8, the specific gravity of the cured sealing compound shall be not greater than 1.65 for Class 1 or 1.50 for Class 2.

When tested as specified in 4.8.9, the cured sealing compound shall not in itself induce corrosion and shall protect the substrate metal. There shall be no visible evidence of corrosion at the metal-sealant interface.
When tested at temperatures and in accordance with the method specified in 4.8.10, the cured sealing compound shall withstand the bend test without cracking, checking, or separating from the panel.

When tested at temperatures and in accordance with the method specified in 4.8.11, the cured sealing compound shall not blister, crack, or show evidence of "blowing" at rest or when wrapped 180° on a mandrel.
The hardness, after exposure, shall be within -5 to +15 points of the original "as cured" hardness.
The tensile strength of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 200 pounds per square inch (psi) for Class 1 or 250 psi for Class 2 (see 4.8.12).
The tensile strength of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 200 pounds per square inch (psi) for Class 1 or 250 psi for Class 2 (see 4.8.12).
The elongation of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 150 percent for Class 1 or 250 percent for Class 2 (see 4.8.12).
The elongation of the cured sealing compound shall be not less than 150 percent for Class 1 or 250 percent for Class 2 (see 4.8.12).

When tested as specified in 4.8.13, the peel strength of the cured sealing compound, as received and after immersion, shall be not less than 15 pounds per inch width (piw) for Class 1 or 20 piw for Class 2.

When tested as specified in 4.8.13, the peel strength of the cured sealing compound, as received and after immersion, shall be not less than 15 pounds per inch width (piw) for Class 1 or 20 piw for Class 2.
All specimens shall exhibit 100 percent cohesive failure.

testler.test_adi: Anchorage (wet tape test, Type III only)

sinir.orijinal_metin: When tested as specified in 4.8.14, the cured sealing compound shall show no more than a slight widening (1/8 inch) of the scratch.

A second coat of the sealing compound, applied over a freshly cured coating of the materials specified in 4.8.15, shall show satisfactory bonding with no lifting, blistering, loss of adhesion, or other coating irregularities.
When tested as specified in 4.8.15, the adhesion strength of the compound shall be not less than 10 piw for Types I, II, and IV; Type III repairability shall be as specified in 3.3.2.9.
When tested as specified in 4.8.16, the air content of the cured sealing compound shall be not greater than 4 percent.

When tested as specified in 4.8.17, the base compound and curing agent shall show no hardening, separating, or settling of material after being stored for 9 months. After the storage period, the mixed sealing compound shall meet the requirements for flow (3.3.1.4), application life (3.3.1.5), tack-free time (3.3.1.6), and hardness (3.3.2.1).
In order to interface with existing equipment and meet the required storage characteristics, the unit of issue for the sealing compound shall be in kits as described below.
Skin contact warning labels shall be added by the manufacturer.

kosul.orijinal_metin: A 1-quart sample of sealing compound and the appropriate amount of curing agent shall be stored for 9 months at 77° ± 6° F (25° ± 3° C).

kosullar.aciklama: The minimum application time, in hours, for each type and class is indicated by a dash number (e.g. Type I-1/2 = 1/2 hour).
